summary: SLA template consolidation and auto-generation for routing-engine-v2
description:
Issue summary: Consolidate legacy SLA templates used by Support Tooling and migrate them to the new routing-engine-v2 template schema. Implement an automated generator to produce routing macros and per-queue SLA configs so workspace teams can opt-in without manual edits.

Background: During the routing engine v2 rollout we kept backward compatibility by maintaining a set of legacy SLA templates in support-tooling. As more queues migrated, discrepancies emerged between template fields, causing mismatches between SLA calculation (console) and route assignments (engine). This manifests as SLA alerts firing incorrectly and inconsistent per-customer routing.

Impact: Internal support tooling reports (SLO/SLA dashboards) are showing ~8% of queues with mismatched SLA windows and 5% with missing on-call contact macros. If not resolved, risk of missed escalations and incorrect SLA reporting for internal incidents.

Scope: - Audit all existing SLA templates in support-tooling repo and legacy database. - Define canonical v2 template schema and mapping rules. - Build an automated template generator that emits: per-queue SLA JSON, routing macros, and a release artifact for the routing-engine-v2 config store. - Add reporting checks and a PR pipeline job to validate new templates on change.

Desired outcome: A one-click migration path for queues to opt into v2 templates, automated generation of macros, and a nightly report showing remaining queues on legacy format.

investigation_notes: Inventory: 142 templates found; 34 used by active queues in prod. Differences cluster around field naming, timezone handling, and contact macros.
Hypothesis: Mismatches are caused by direct edits to legacy templates in db without corresponding repo change. Confirmed ~12 manual edits since 2025-11.
Findings: routing-engine-v2 rejects templates that lack 'slo.targets' array; legacy templates often used 'slo_target' singular. Mapping rule defined to convert singular->array.
Telemetry: Alerting noise correlates with queues where last_template_update != last_repo_commit (delta > 7 days).
